title: Implement exact physical normalized polynomial products and Fourier composition
body:
I complete the normalized-product handoff from [PR3640](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3640). I implement exact physical `Q_p(uv/r)` on complete Gaussian polynomial packets, then execute two forward Fourier calls, that product, the opposite call and an exact M scale. I preserve the input packets and restore the fixed tape owners.

I use a concrete shrinking Karatsuba word engine, sequential DIF/DIT complex FFTs and certified inward Machin/Taylor twiddles. With `Q=2p+2(ell+1)+ceil(log2(12(ell+1)+2))+3`, I bound scaled error below 1/8 and recover exact ordinary integer coefficients before negacyclic subtraction. I charge `O(CMr(ell+1)p^(8/5)+rp^3+(A+p+log(C+1))^3)` time, including setup, and O(V) space. Under A=Theta(p), epsilon=.997 gives online power .603 per input bit, within the inherited Fourier allowance.

The convolution caller returns width `p+2+A` at unchanged precision p, with error below `4sqrt(2)M2^-p` from `(f*g)/(rM)`. The caller needs a disk margin before narrowing. I leave the selected frontier unchanged and retain the inherited supplier/refinement assumptions; I do not establish the Gaussian/CRT/integer join or a new integer exponent.

I started from canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6, and recorded the expansion gate and overlap checks in [Discussion3664](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664). This PR changes only `research/physical-ring-product/`.

Current head: `62264289adb01f3ba4930cd0154c75887f96203c`. I corrected a cost citation after tracing the next interface: the complete Fourier power is .99827619697, while 332353/332929 is the primitive power. The product's .603 allowance fits the corrected bound. I now bind the budget check to PR3640's authenticated calculation. I changed the proof, budget checker and documentation; I retained the data arithmetic and lifecycle code. I verified the corrected export and hosted CI on this head.

Validation at `62264289adb01f3ba4930cd0154c75887f96203c`:

- Eight registered suites passed locally: sources, budget, words, twiddles, fft, product, convolution and failures.
- I checked scalar products through 257 bits, 23 certified twiddles, complete product packets, 11 physical fault controls and a complete 16-Gaussian convolution with nonzero rounding. I used the actual direct/literal q2 Fourier child for that composition; production GL64/O73 execution remains outside this receipt.
- Metadata, source-history and committed-byte preflight passed. I replayed all eight commands from the corrected official export outside Git on Darwin arm64, Python 3.12.13, and checked that all 27 regular files, including the receipt, remained byte-for-byte unchanged. The full convolution took 103.393 seconds in that replay.
- Official export SHA256: `c03d4b056ccd3db860c93579f6525e0bb1baea31cff879eb07135c99432ef159`; receipt SHA256: `39c6eb4f1c2d38fdf8e44ae5c6b16bfe5315ff796ac60f1f6e48161ad3e2bab4`.
- Hosted [CI39154288761](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39154288761) passed all eight suites and the unchanged-input check. I verified that its merge tree equals the published head tree `37c7ce724ecb928d62c21bc29d890433b2bd667c`.

Read `README.md`, `PROOF.md` and `EVIDENCE.md` for the contract, proof and checked scope. Reproduce with `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/physical-ring-product`.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including source-analysis agents. I credit the standard Karatsuba and radix-two FFT algorithms, Mason Hale's PR2313 interval reference, Dugongue's PR2790 multiplier/ABI precedent, PR3640's retained source chain, and source06's Nussbaumer/Quandalle, Harvey/van der Hoeven and OpenAI notices. I claim no independent human review or formal-kernel verification.
